source.title: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models using Multi-Clip Video
source.authors: Choongwon Kang; Seungjong Sun; Hyunmin Jun; Jang-Hyun Kim

page_placements.theme: Visual, audio and combined-modality safety gaps

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests jailbreak vulnerability in video-capable multimodal models, a new setting and attack type relative to the claim; the reported outcomes do not test the listed fine-tuning or token-depth mechanisms.
record.gate_note: The paper measures harmful-response rates for explicit and typography-in-video attacks as clip count and visual-input conditions change. It does not fine-tune models, measure aligned/base per-token KL, prefill model context with compliant tokens, test adversarial suffixes or decoding changes, edit weights, or study why safety would be shallow. Rows are outcomes for this paper's video attacks and defenses, recorded under fits_no_version rather than as evidence for a listed version.
record.test_reason: The paper measures jailbreak success of multi-clip video inputs on video MLLMs. It does no fine-tuning (V1, V2), no aligned/base per-token KL (V3), no prefilling, suffix or decoding change (V4), no parameter localization (V5), no test of causes of shallowness (V6), and no deepening training (V7). The attack prompt asks for a fixed compliant opening ('Welcome to Earth... Step 1:'), but this is a prompt-level instruction, not a prefill, and is held constant rather than varied. Qi et al. 2023 (an original) is cited only for the GPT-judge 1–5 harmfulness scoring. The reader's 'tests/T3' contradicts its own finding that every version is not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that video inputs are more jailbreak-prone than images, and that ASR rises with dynamic, diverse multi-clip content. They add that last-token hidden states shift toward the harmless region as clip count grows (PCA, Figure 4). They propose single-frame image filtering as a defense, which they call indirect rather than a fundamental fix.
record.recipe_differences: Uses generated multi-clip videos and explicit or typography-concealed jailbreak prompts; no fine-tuning, KL measurement, token-prefill, or weight-edit recipe is used.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies with model, attack type, clip count, modality, dynamic versus static content, and repeated versus diverse clips. The paper also reports model-dependent results for defenses and OCR-sensitive implicit attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: Video-MLLM ASR is highest at 4 clips in Table 2 for all eight models. Increases range from large (Qwen2.5-VL-7B explicit, 50.75 to 68.70) to negligible (LLaVA-Video-7B explicit, 66.58 to 66.85).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More diverse multi-clip video inputs raise harmful-response rates in video MLLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Image-frame, static-video and repeated-clip inputs give lower ASR than diverse dynamic clips. For Qwen3-VL-8B and InternVL3.5-8B, static video is nearly equal to the original.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Video jailbreak vulnerability depends on dynamics and contextual diversity, not input length alone.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-frame image filtering using the target model cuts average ASR from 67.34 to 17.37. Prompt defenses vary by model; the safety prompt has no effect on LLaVA-Video-7B.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The main ASR is judged by GPT-4o-mini, with score 5 counted as success; human comparison covers 200 randomly sampled samples and reports correlation 0.6229 (std = 0.069). The video dataset is generated and manually filtered; ASR uncertainty is not reported for individual model-condition values. The paper itself notes the tested videos are short and cover at most five clips.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row cap, omitted Table 2's 2- and 3-clip values; Table 3's 1-, 2-, and 3-clip comparator values and reported averages; and additional results in Tables 6–9 (8-fps checks, HunyuanVideo-1.5 generation, five-clip results, and closed-source models). The selected Table 2 endpoints and the Table 3/4 comparisons retain the main clip-count and condition contrasts.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or aligned-versus-base comparison.
No prefilled compliant tokens, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. The fixed requested opening is not varied, so its effect on refusal is not isolated.
No test of whether data or objective causes shallowness.
No deepening training or durability test.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given because no version is tested. Qi et al. 2023 appears only as the source of the judge scoring scheme. The closed-model results (Table 9), five-clip results (Table 8) and HunyuanVideo results (Table 7) are omitted from the rows, but they also bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or measurement of its effect on refusal.
No benign-data fine-tuning or measurement of its effect on harmful compliance.
No aligned/base comparison or per-token KL measurement.
The study uses video-based attacks with a prompt that requests a compliant opening, but does not prefill the model context with that opening; suffix attacks and decoding changes are also not tested.
No parameter or rank localization, ablation, or weight edit.
No test of whether data or training objectives cause token-depth shallowness.
No training to deepen safety across response tokens or test of its durability.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Qi et al. (2023) is cited for the evaluation framework and harmfulness scoring; the study neither tests nor relies on its fine-tuning finding.

tranche.reason: The experiments vary video content and clip count; none tests V1–V7 or uses a shallow-alignment finding as a tool. PCA of final-input-token representations does not measure response-position concentration.

source_check.notes: All listed values match Table 2; four clips gives the highest ASR within its one-to-four-clip comparison for every model and attack setting. The attacks request a response format but do not prefill generated tokens, so they do not establish V4.
